candidates.name: PTC-readthrough-restore-full-length
candidates.biological_hypothesis: Because the only defect is a single premature termination codon in exon 55, forcing ribosomal readthrough of that codon would produce full-length, correctly folded Dp427m including the cysteine-rich and C-terminal domains, restoring the whole dystrophin-glycoprotein complex rather than a partial surrogate. This is the most proximal possible intervention short of gene editing.
candidates.target_or_process: Translation termination at the exon 55 PTC (eukaryotic release factor complex eRF1/eRF3); secondarily nonsense-mediated decay (UPF1/SMG1) which limits available template
candidates.desired_perturbation: Partial, selective suppression of termination at the PTC (gain of full-length dystrophin output); optional concomitant partial NMD inhibition to raise mutant transcript abundance

evidence_for.statement: Ataluren promotes readthrough of DMD premature stop codons and increased dystrophin immunostaining (dystrophin/spectrin ratio) in 23/38 boys after 28 days in a Phase 2a biopsy study — direct human proof that readthrough can generate dystrophin protein in nonsense DMD.
Nonsense mutations account for ~10-15% of DMD and readthrough is an established, mutation-class-specific therapeutic concept with an approved agent in some jurisdictions.
Retrospective Spanish cohort of 28 nonsense-mutation DMD boys reported ~3-year later loss of ambulation in ataluren-treated versus untreated patients (all on corticosteroids).

Ataluren acts by competitive inhibition of release-factor-complex-catalysed termination, and readthrough efficiency is strongly determined by the identity of the stop codon and its immediately adjacent mRNA sequence context; combinations with aminoglycosides (G418) or anticodon-edited aa-tRNAs can be additive. This gives a concrete in vitro route to test whether THIS exon 55 codon context is permissive, and a combination fallback if ataluren alone is weak.

Suppressor/anticodon-engineered tRNA and NMD-modulating oligonucleotides are an emerging second generation of readthrough modalities, relevant if the small molecule is insufficient for this codon context.

evidence_against.statement: Readthrough magnitude is inconsistent across patients and mutations, and reported clinical benefit of ataluren comes largely from open-label/registry and subgroup analyses rather than a clearly positive confirmatory randomised endpoint; the regulatory status of ataluren in Europe has been contested. I did not retrieve the confirmatory trial or regulatory documents in this session, so treat the efficacy magnitude as unresolved.
If the exon 55 PTC is efficiently degraded by NMD there may be insufficient mRNA template, predicting non-response. No exon-55-specific NMD or readthrough data were retrieved.

candidates.key_biological_uncertainty: Two measurable quantities decide this approach: (a) abundance of the mutant DMD transcript in patient myotubes/urine-derived cells (NMD efficiency), and (b) readthrough permissiveness of this exact stop codon plus its +1/-1 nucleotide context, testable in a reconstituted translation or dual-luciferase reporter carrying the patient's exon 55 sequence.

candidates.name: Exon-45-55-multiskip-bypass
candidates.biological_hypothesis: A PTC cannot be corrected by single-exon skipping, but excising the entire exon 45-55 block removes the mutated exon and is frame-neutral, yielding an internally deleted dystrophin that retains both the actin-binding N-terminus and the cysteine-rich/C-terminal domains. Patients with naturally occurring del45-55 generally have a mild Becker phenotype, so the product is expected to be functional.
candidates.target_or_process: DMD pre-mRNA splicing across exons 45-55 (exonic/intronic splice enhancers and branch points of each targeted exon)
candidates.desired_perturbation: Induced skipping of the 11-exon block to remove the exon 55 PTC while restoring an in-frame transcript

evidence_for.statement: Systemic delivery of an ASO (PMO) cocktail inducing exon 45-55 skipping has been established as a tractable in vivo protocol in mdx52 mice, with evaluable dystrophin restoration.

Multi-exon skipping across 45-55 is explicitly analysed as a broad-applicability strategy covering a large share of DMD mutations in a systematic UMD-DMD database analysis of single, double and multi-exon skipping strategies.

Restoration of dystrophin protein by inducing the 45-55 multi-exon deletion was demonstrated in DMD patient-derived iPSCs with three distinct mutations, supporting that the 45-55-deleted product is expressed and detectable (achieved there by genome editing, which is out of scope as a therapy but informative about the protein product).

Because exon 55 lies inside the 45-55 block and the block is reported as frame-neutral, this is the smallest known skip geometry that removes the mutated exon while preserving the C-terminal anchoring domains.

evidence_against.statement: A cocktail of ~10-11 ASOs must act on the same transcript in the same nucleus to yield a single in-frame product, so the efficiency penalty is multiplicative; this is a far harder pharmacology and regulatory problem than approved single-exon PMOs, and no clinical multi-skip ASO exists.

Approved exon-skipping ASOs achieve only low single-digit percent dystrophin in muscle and have unclear functional benefit; a multi-skip would plausibly do worse per transcript. Muscle/heart delivery remains the limiting factor for all naked PMO chemistry.

candidates.key_biological_uncertainty: Whether any achievable in vivo concentration of a multi-ASO cocktail (or a conjugated/peptide-targeted chemistry) produces enough fully 45-55-skipped transcript to matter; and whether a smaller frame-restoring block around exon 55 exists, which should be computed from the patient's transcript before committing.

candidates.name: Downstream-degeneration-brake
candidates.biological_hypothesis: Much of the irreversible disability in DMD comes from the downstream consequences of dystrophin loss — necrosis, failed regeneration, TGF-beta-driven endomysial fibrosis and fatty replacement — not from the absence of dystrophin per se at any single moment. Blunting that secondary cascade should slow functional decline independently of genotype, and is the only arm that remains available if readthrough proves non-viable for this allele. It also protects the tissue substrate on which any later dystrophin-restoring therapy depends.
candidates.target_or_process: Class I/II HDACs and the fibro-adipogenic / TGF-beta-driven remodelling program in dystrophic muscle; broader inflammation and regeneration pathways
candidates.desired_perturbation: Reduce fibrosis, necrosis and fatty replacement; increase the fraction of contractile muscle tissue and compensatory regeneration

evidence_for.statement: In the randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 EPIDYS trial, the HDAC inhibitor givinostat reduced decline in four-stair-climb performance versus placebo in ambulant DMD boys on corticosteroids — a positive controlled functional outcome for a genotype-agnostic, dystrophin-independent mechanism.
Givinostat was approved in the USA in March 2024 for DMD in patients aged 6+ irrespective of the underlying genetic variant, so this arm is available to an exon 55 nonsense patient today.

Paired muscle biopsies in 20 DMD boys treated >=12 months showed givinostat significantly increased the muscle-tissue fraction and reduced fibrotic tissue, necrosis and fatty replacement — direct human target-engagement evidence on the pathology this hypothesis targets.
Open-label extension with up to >8 years exposure in 194 patients showed a safety profile consistent with prior studies and post hoc natural-history comparisons suggesting sustained benefit.

evidence_against.statement: In the 12-month biopsy study, histological improvement was not accompanied by improvement in functional tests, so histological target engagement does not automatically translate into function.

This approach does not correct the causal defect; it can at best slow decline, and benefit is likely capped by pre-existing fibrosis and fat replacement. Long-term comparisons so far rest on open-label/post hoc natural-history analyses.
Cardiac and respiratory failure dominate mortality, and the pivotal evidence is in ambulant skeletal-muscle function; cardiac benefit of this mechanism was not retrieved.

candidates.key_biological_uncertainty: Whether slowing fibro-fatty remodelling preserves enough tissue, and for long enough, to change respiratory and cardiac outcomes rather than only ambulatory timed tests — and whether combining it with a dystrophin-restoring arm is additive.

conclusion_note: The upstream biology (dystrophin absence) is solid, so three mechanistically distinct arms can be stated with confidence: proximal readthrough, frame-bypass by 45-55 multi-skip, and a genotype-agnostic downstream brake. What is NOT established is the exon-55-specific layer that decides between arms 1 and 2: NMD efficiency for this allele and readthrough permissiveness of this exact stop-codon context. Both are cheap, decisive bench questions (patient myotube or urine-derived-cell transcript quantification; dual-luciferase or reconstituted-translation reporter carrying the patient's exon 55 context per PMID 40156864) and should be done before any modality commitment. Arm 3 is actionable immediately and does not depend on that result. Arm 2 is the weakest on deliverability, not on biology. Decision support for researchers, not medical advice.
